text:
**Review Result**

Quality score: **6.5/10**. The code is small, readable, and covered by a decent pytest suite, but I would not approve it as-is because the database update logic can corrupt historical job state and the parser accepts invalid resource data.

**Findings**

- High: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) lines 70-84: Older terminal records can overwrite newer terminal records during out-of-order ingest.
- Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:129) lines 129-134 and [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:40) lines 40-41: Unknown or typo states are accepted and treated as terminal lifecycle states.
- Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:111) lines 111-112, 149-163: Negative CPU/GPU allocations are accepted, producing negative usage reports.
- Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) lines 13-27: SQLite schema has no `CHECK` constraints, so invalid counts/states can be inserted outside the parser.
- Medium: [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) lines 14, 58-70, 79-106: Report queries filter on `COALESCE(end,start,submit)` without supporting indexes, so production-sized accounting tables will full-scan.
- Low: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118) lines 118-125 and [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:113) lines 113-121: Offset-aware timestamps are accepted but later compared as text, which can misorder mixed-offset data.
- Low: [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:99) lines 99-103, 121-126, 138-143, 176-180: SQLite operational errors are uncaught, so locked/corrupt/unwritable DBs produce tracebacks instead of clean CLI failures.
- Low: [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:13) lines 13-23: Project has tests but no configured linting, typing, coverage, or CI-quality gates.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q` passed: **61 passed**. `compileall` passed when `PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX` was redirected; direct `compileall` failed only because this workspace would not allow writing `__pycache__`.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change scope: **180 LOC** including fixes and regression tests.

Bottom line: **No**, I would not approve this PR as-is.

issues.description: Older terminal records can overwrite newer terminal records during out-of-order ingest.
Unknown or typo states are accepted and treated as terminal lifecycle states.
Negative CPU/GPU allocations are accepted and can produce negative usage reports.
SQLite schema lacks CHECK constraints to protect data integrity outside the parser.
Report queries filter on unindexed COALESCE expressions and will full-scan large job tables.
Offset-aware timestamps are accepted but later compared as text, which can misorder mixed-offset data.
SQLite operational errors are uncaught, causing tracebacks instead of clean CLI failures.
No linting, typing, coverage, or CI-quality gates are configured.
